observation.visible_scene: A close-up, low-light shot of a small burning fire. The background is dark and out of focus. In the foreground, a pile of charred wood fragments and glowing red embers sits in fixed positions, with a small secondary flame flickering at the left edge. A dominant flame rises in the center-right, showing a blue base at the fuel line and a bright yellow-white body above it. The framing of the sticks and embers stays identical throughout, indicating a static camera.
visible_changes: The main flame continuously flickers and deforms: its tip grows taller and shorter, leans left or right, and repeatedly splits into two or three lobes (e.g., an M-shape around frames 2, 9, 12, 15, 20, 28, 31, 39) before merging back into a single pointed tongue (e.g., frames 5, 7, 10, 22-26, 30, 34-35, 40-41).
The blue base beneath the bright flame pulses in size and intensity, sometimes broad, sometimes thin, but remains present the whole excerpt.
The small flame on the left varies in brightness and height, flaring and dimming without moving its base.
The red glow of the embers shifts slightly in intensity but the ember and stick positions do not translate.
No object moves across the frame and no camera pan/zoom is evident; all visible change is the unsteady combustion of the flames themselves.
outside_clip_unknowns: How the fire was started and what fuel/wood is being burned.
Whether the flames will grow, die down, or be disturbed after the last frame.
The wider environment surrounding the fire (indoor hearth vs. outdoor pit).
uncertain_details: Exact material identity of the charred pieces (wood vs. other fuel) cannot be confirmed.
Any very slight camera vibration is indistinguishable from the flicker of the light, so camera motion is treated as none.
Whether the splitting lobes are separate flame tongues or one tongue bending around the foreground stick edge is not fully resolvable.
